narrative:
The file contains a current proof-of-address document for Joe Bloggs and a solicitor's letter confirming a £100,000 distribution from the estate of his late father, John Bloggs. Those items support compliant source-of-funds and address evidence for those streams.
The source-of-funds evidence remains incomplete for the separate £200,000 gift from Jill Withers. The donor source-of-funds review records that no independent evidence was provided to evidence the origin or accumulation of the funds, but the file nevertheless accepts the gift funds for completion without requesting further donor source-of-funds evidence.
Bank statements cover only about six weeks for an £875,000 overseas-client purchase, below the firm's own six-month requirement for high-value or overseas matters.
The client risk assessment records standard risk, despite firm policy requiring high risk and enhanced due diligence for clients resident outside the UK.
The MLRO interview describes informal source-of-funds verification that does not produce the audit trail required by the firm's own AML procedures.
The source-of-funds schedule is useful because it records the evidence status by stream, but it also records unresolved gaps for the savings and gift evidence.
The PEP screening report names John Bloggs. The estate solicitor's letter identifies John Bloggs as Joe Bloggs' deceased father, so the report appears to screen the wrong person.
